item.title: US Stock Futures Drop as Rising Oil Prices Stoke Inflation Fears
item.description: US stock futures skidded on Tuesday, with traders bracing for interest-rate ‌hikes as renewed Middle East tensions lifted oil prices and bond yields, stoking inflation fears.

item.title: Israel Slashes Interest Rates for Third Consecutive Meeting
item.description: Israel lowered interest rates on Monday, in a decision that comes as exporters push the central bank to do more to counter the shekel’s appreciation.

item.title: China Unlikely to Match ASML’s Top Tool in Next Decade, UBS Says
item.description: China is unlikely to advance its semiconductor manufacturing capabilities fast enough to develop a viable alternative to ASML Holding NV’s cutting-edge extreme ultraviolet technology within the next decade, UBS Group AG analysts predict.

item.title: Fed’s Barr Says Higher Rates Needed If Inflation Doesn’t Cool
item.description: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said the central bank should be prepared to raise interest rates if inflation fails to subside, warning price pressures are at risk of becoming entrenched after being above target for more than five years.

item.title: Roku Launches Its First OLED TVs, With Prices Starting at $999
item.description: Roku Inc. introduced its first self-branded smart TVs with organic light emitting diode, or OLED, display technology, which will lend the new models greater contrast and punchier black levels than previous first-party Roku TVs.

item.title: Chile Economic Activity Posts Biggest Monthly Drop Since 2022
item.description: Chile’s economy contracted much more than expected in July as deadly rainstorms temporarily halted some mining operations, according to the central bank’s main monthly gauge of activity.

item.title: Saudi Video Game Giant Savvy CEO Brian Ward Is Stepping Down
item.description: Savvy Games Group Chief Executive Officer Brian Ward, who oversaw the Saudi Arabian government’s $38 billion investment in the video-game industry, is stepping down, according to a message he sent to staff on Tuesday that was reviewed by Bloomberg News.

item.title: Brazil Economy Loses Steam as High Rates Bite Before Vote
item.description: Brazil’s economy saw a modest expansion in the second quarter after a stronger start to the year as high interest rates dragged on growth ahead of the presidential election.

item.title: A Lucrative Crypto Contract Sets Off New No-Bid Fight for Trump
item.description: The US government awarded a lucrative contract to a crypto analytics firm without putting it up for competitive bidding, sparking a legal fight and opening a new avenue for criticism over the Trump administration’s tendency toward no-bid deals.

item.title: Ares Venture Buys US Student Housing Properties for $435 Million
item.description: The Scion Group and Ares Management Corp. funds bought four US student housing communities for about $435 million, the second deal for the companies’ new partnership.

item.title: Gold Stocks Cap Best August in Decades in Debasement Trade Redux
item.description: An almost-vertical rally in gold-miner stocks in the past month is whetting the appetite of investors who have been whipsawed by messages from Washington policymakers.

item.title: Hormuz Oil Flow Recovery Imperiled by Renewed Tanker Attacks
item.description: Higher levels of exports seen recently are looking tenuous.

item.title: Goldman Sees Room for South Africa Asset Rally on Credit Upgrade
item.description: Markets are not pricing in the probability of South Africa’s return to investment grade, leaving scope for government bonds, stocks and the rand to rally, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc.

item.title: Indian Students Cancel March After Court Orders Cases be Dropped
item.description: India’s top court ordered criminal cases be dropped against students who took part in mass protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party in July, prompting the group to call off a planned march later this week.

item.title: Nvidia’s MediaTek Investment Marks the Next AI Chipmaking Champion to Watch
item.description: Nvidia and Google are investing in Taiwan’s unheralded chipmaker

item.title: China Latest: Beijing Revamps Home-Sales System That Worsened Its Meltdown
item.description: Developers once relied on cash from selling homes before they were built

item.title: China’s Manufacturing Strength and AI
item.description: AI-related demand is providing tailwinds for Chinese exporters

item.title: YouTube Inks Amazon Partnership to Boost Online Shopping Bet
item.description: YouTube has tapped Amazon.com Inc. as its newest affiliate partner in YouTube Shopping, part of the video giant’s push to prioritize e-commerce as one of its next big bets.

item.title: Africa Faces El Niño With Less Room to Weather Shock, IIF Says
item.description: Africa is heading into a strong El Niño from a weaker economic position than the last one a decade ago, adding to price pressures triggered by the Iran war, the Institute of International Finance said.

item.title: Trillion-Dollar Dislocation Hides in Calm Credit Markets
item.description: As government bond yields across the world erupt, corporate credit has rarely looked calmer. Yet even in that market, about $1 trillion of bonds are telling a much different story.

item.title: Bank of Canada Set to Hold as Trade War Creates New Dilemma for Tiff Macklem
item.description: The Bank of Canada is likely to hold borrowing costs steady, as an escalation in the trade war with the US threatens the economic recovery while adding to inflation risks.

item.title: AI Job Risks Spread to PR, Web Development and Hotel Workers
item.description: The US job market isn’t improving

item.title: El Niño and Disease Threaten West Africa’s Cocoa Harvest Again
item.description: Simon Essah walks through his cocoa farm in southwest Ghana, pointing to trees scarred by black pod disease, the latest in a series of threats plaguing his crop this year.

item.title: Salesforce Backs Software Firm HiBob at $3.2 Billion Value
item.description: Salesforce Inc. is investing in human resources software company HiBob as part of a more than $160 million funding round that values the startup at over $3.2 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Felix Pago Raises $200 Million to Expand Into Financial Services
item.description: Money-transfer startup Felix Pago raised $200 million to expand beyond remittances and offer services such as lending and savings to Latin American immigrants in the US.

item.title: Dyson Announces $499 CameraJet Smart Toothbrush With AI, Built-In Camera
item.description: Dyson Ltd. introduced a $499 toothbrush that uses artificial intelligence and a built-in camera to give real-time feedback, the latest in a growing subset of gadgets that put AI and video in sometimes unconventional places.

item.title: Gilts Lead Global Bond Selloff as Traders Play Catch Up
item.description: Gilts led a selloff in global government bonds on Tuesday as investors played catch up after the UK market was closed for a holiday.

item.title: Bond Slide Spreads to Emerging Markets on Fed Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: A global bond selloff spread to emerging markets as investors dumped the riskier debt on expectations that the Federal Reserve will increase US interest rates later this month.

item.title: China Freezes China Court Freezes Nexperia Assets in Fight Over Dutch Chipmaker
item.description: Nexperia BV’s owner Wingtech Technology Co. said a Chinese court froze 2.14 billion yuan ($318 million) worth of assets held by the Dutch chipmaker, the latest in a protracted tussle for control of the company.

item.title: Euro-Zone Inflation Jumps to Highest in Almost Three Years
item.description: Euro-area inflation quickened to the highest level in almost three years, cementing the case for an interest-rate hike by the European Central Bank next week.
